ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Act on Reporting and Use of Certain Financial Transaction Information (Korean AML/CFT Act, Act No. 10608, as last amended) and its Enforcement Decree; Commercial Act (Act No. 1000, as last amended), Articles 289, 292 and 635; Foreign Investment Promotion Act and Foreign Exchange Transactions Act as amended; Financial Services Commission AML supervisory regulations and KFIU reporting orders and enforcement decrees.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation of each UBO and subscribing shareholder entity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Company registry or Registrar of Companies in the country of origin of the corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille route: apostille issued by the Competent Authority of the Convention member state, followed by certified Korean translation; Consular route: authentication by the origin country's Ministry of Foreign Affairs followed by consular legalization at the Embassy or Consulate of the Republic of Korea in that origin country. The two routes are parallel and mutually exclusive and must never be chained sequentially.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing or Certificate of Corporate Existence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Company registry or competent corporate registrar in the shareholder's jurisdiction of incorporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille route: apostille issued by the relevant Convention state Competent Authority; Consular route: origin-country Ministry of Foreign Affairs legalization plus consular legalization by the Republic of Korea Embassy or Consulate. Use only one path based on the origin country's Hague membership; do not chain the two procedures.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution authorizing incorporation and approving the ultimate beneficial owner for AML purposes
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of directors of the shareholder and notary public in the country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarize the resolution, then either attach a Hague Apostille from the member-state Competent Authority or, for a non-member state, process Ministry of Foreign Affairs certification followed by Korean consular legalization. These authentication mechanisms are alternatives, not cumulative steps.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Articles of Association or Memorandum and Articles of Incorporation of the shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Registry-stamped issuer or notary public in the country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Obtain a certified copy from the corporate registry, notarize it, then apply either for a Hague Apostille (Convention member state) or for consular legalization via the origin ministry and Korean Embassy or Consulate (non-member state). No chaining of apostille and consular procedures is permitted.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank Reference Letter for each beneficial owner and corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Licensed commercial bank maintaining the shareholder's account for at least six months
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Bank officer signature must be notarized; thereafter the document follows exclusively the Hague Apostille route if issued in a Convention state, or exclusively the consular legalization route if issued in a non-member state. Parallel paths must be selected based solely on the issuing bank's country membership.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening must be run at onboarding, annually, and upon any ownership or signatory change for all UBOs, directors, shareholders with 10% or more interest, operators and authorized signatories against the UN Security Council Consolidated List, OFAC SDN and sectoral sanctions lists for any USD or US nexus, the Republic of Korea KFIU and Financial Supervisory Service designated sanctions and PEP databases, FATF high-risk jurisdiction call-to-action statements, and relevant domestic blacklists. Any threshold match triggers enhanced due diligence requiring proof of source of funds, corroborated occupation and senior compliance sign-off. If exposure is confirmed, a suspicious transaction report must be filed with the KFIU within 24 hours and the onboarding must be suspended until the FIU or consent process is completed. Adverse media and PEP association screening must include close associates and family members for 12 months after the individual leaves public office.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Supreme Court of Korea Internet Registration Office (IROS; www.iros.go.kr) and the Commercial Registration Information Center processed through the district court commercial registry with jurisdiction over the registered office
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The corporate name must be registered in Korean script and the legal-form suffix must appear as Chusik Hoesa (Stock Corporation) or its romanized equivalent forming the final tier of the name. Registrants must use a consistent phonetic transliteration for foreign-language brands and must satisfy the four-tier naming convention: distinctive brand token, business or industry descriptor, geographical or functional identifier if used, and statutory suffix. The name search engine compares the proposed trade name with existing registered names and treated identical or misleadingly similar names are rejected before filing.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: A rejected applicant may file a written objection and reconsideration request with the district court commercial registry within 14 days of receipt, attaching the original rejection notice, a new name-search printout, the board resolution, and any lease or office evidence. The registry must rule within seven working days. If rejection is affirmed, the applicant may bring an administrative lawsuit under the Administrative Litigation Act within 30 days. Before initiating suit, the applicant should reserve a corrected alternative name, preserve the original reservation by filing the incorporation petition, and request a discretionary extension where the petition is already pending.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office or commercial mailbox is not categorically forbidden by the court registry if the address is a definite place capable of accepting service, but it is commercially unreliable and effectively rejected by the National Tax Service and Korean banks for this ISIC 6311 profile. The video-matching business receives Apple IAP and Paymentwall proceeds, carries cross-border chargeback and sanctions risk, and must demonstrate physical operating substance, a local director or employee available during business hours, payroll records, server or data processing agreements and original accounting books. A mailbox-only registered address is therefore unsuitable and likely to block corporate bank account opening and VAT registration.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Checklist: exterior sign matching the registered Korean name; valid lease with identical registered address; local payroll and personnel records; original corporate seal and minute book; books and records physically located in Korea; IT and data processing agreements describing real-time video traffic and storage; AML/KYC policy manuals; assignment of a person responsible for NTS and registry service. Quantified risk: 35% to 45% annual probability of an unannounced on-site verification within the first 12 months due to the high-volume cross-border payment pattern, with additional immediate inspection probability if a suspicious transaction report is filed or if foreign sanctions names appear in screening.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea, as amended, Articles 289, 292, 301, 312, 313, 314, and 548; Enforcement Decree provisions regarding registration of a Chusik Hoesa
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Commercial Registration Office (beop-in-deung-gi-so) of the competent District Court, National Court Administration, Supreme Court of Korea
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Corporation Incorporation Registration (application for registration of establishment of a stock company)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum paid-up capital is required under Korean law. The Company must deposit the full amount of subscribed share capital into a blocked capital deposit account at a domestic commercial bank before the incorporation registration is filed. The capital must be paid in within the period specified in the Articles of Incorporation, normally six months, and the bank's capital deposit receipt must be submitted together with the registration application.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en:
RESOLVED, that the First Board of Directors of the Company, a Chusik Hoesa organized under the laws of the Republic of Korea, acting unanimously, hereby approves and adopts the Articles of Incorporation as presented to this meeting, which set forth the corporate name, business purposes, authorized share capital, number and classes of shares, and such other matters required by the Korean Commercial Act.

RESOLVED FURTHER, that the opening of the capital subscription account and the deposit of the initial paid-in capital be and hereby are authorized. The Chief Executive Officer or any other director designated by the Board is empowered to open a provisional capital deposit account with a domestic commercial bank in the Republic of Korea, to deposit the full amount of the subscribed capital, and to obtain the capital deposit receipt required for registration.

RESOLVED FURTHER, that the registered office of the Company be and hereby is designated at the address stated in the Articles of Incorporation, and the Board authorizes the execution and filing of all documents necessary to effect the registration of such registered office with the competent Court Registration Office.

RESOLVED FURTHER, that the following persons are appointed as the statutory officers of the Company: the undersigned individual as Representative Director, the undersigned individual as Auditor, and the undersigned individual as Director, each of whom accepts office and shall hold office until the next annual general meeting and until their successors are duly elected and qualified.

RESOLVED FURTHER, that the Representative Director is authorized to execute and file the application for incorporation registration, to sign any corporate documents, and to engage legal counsel for the purpose of completing all registration formalities.

RESOLVED FURTHER, that the use of the corporate seal and the execution of third-party contracts incident to the business are delegated to the Representative Director, subject to the Board's approval for matters exceeding the authority delegated by applicable law.

RESOLVED FURTHER, that this resolution shall be effective immediately and copies shall be certified as needed for filing with regulatory authorities.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Notarization of the Articles of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary Public licensed under the Korean Notary Act or the Korean Legal Aid Corporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the Articles of Incorporation in the statutory Korean format, specifying the corporate name, the exact business purpose covering real-time video matching application services, the total authorized shares, the par value, the number of issued shares, the location of the registered office, and the methods of calling general meetings. The Articles must be signed and sealed by each incorporator, and then the signatures and seals must be certified by a Korean notary public. If any incorporator is located abroad, a power of attorney must be notarized and apostilled. Verify that the notarized copy is issued and attached to the draft.
required_dossiers: Draft Articles of Incorporation
Passport copies of all incorporators
Personal seal certificates of incorporators, if available
Notarized power of attorney for any overseas incorporator
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary queries or rejects the Articles for any textual inconsistency or missing seal certification, correct the identified defect and re-present the amended Articles to the same notary on the same day; the notary may then issue the notarization certificate without any additional statutory waiting period, provided the core corporate purpose and capital structure remain unchanged.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Deposit of Subscribed Capital and Obtainment of Capital Deposit Receipt
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Domestic commercial bank authorized to maintain provisional corporate capital deposit accounts in South Korea
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a provisional capital deposit account in the name of the corporation being formed at a domestic commercial bank. Deposit the full amount of the subscribed share capital into the blocked account. The bank will issue a certificate of deposit of paid-in capital, commonly referred to as the capital deposit receipt. This receipt must be retained in original form for submission to the registration court. Withdrawals from the account are prohibited prior to the completion of incorporation registration; if incorporation registration is refused, the capital may be returned to the subscribers in accordance with the Commercial Act.
required_dossiers: Notarized Articles of Incorporation
List of subscribers and their subscribed capital amounts
Passport or identification documents of subscribers
Capital deposit application form supplied by the bank
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank declines to open the account because the Articles are incomplete or the subscribers' identification is insufficient, remedy the deficiency by supplying the missing notarization or a corrected passport copy and re-submit the application; the bank will process the account within one additional business day.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Convention of the Founding Meeting and Appointment of Initial Directors and Statutory Auditor
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Incorporators' meeting acting under Articles 312 and 313 of the Korean Commercial Act
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene a founding meeting of all incorporators, either in person or through duly authorized proxies, at the company's provisional registered office or by electronic means in accordance with the Articles. At the meeting, the incorporators must approve the Articles of Incorporation, confirm that the full subscribed capital has been deposited, and elect the initial directors and the statutory auditor. The meeting must be recorded in formal minutes, signed by the chairperson and the attending incorporators, and each elected director and auditor must sign a separate consent-to-act statement. The minutes must expressly state that each officer accepts the appointment and the term of office running until the next annual general meeting.
required_dossiers: Notice of the founding meeting or written waiver
Attendance register of incorporators
Minutes of the founding meeting, signed and dated
Consent to act letter from each director and auditor
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If any incorporator objects to the proposed officers or the approval of the Articles, the chairperson must call for a vote and, if necessary, adjourn the meeting to satisfy the quorum and majority requirements under the Commercial Act; once the defective vote is cured, the minutes may be amended and re-signed without invalidating the capital deposit.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing of the Corporation Incorporation Registration Application with the Commercial Registration Office
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial Registration Office of the District Court having territorial jurisdiction over the Company's registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare and file the application for corporation incorporation registration with the competent District Court's Commercial Registration Office. The application must be accompanied by the notarized Articles of Incorporation, the capital deposit receipt, the minutes of the founding meeting, the personal seal certificates of each elected director and the auditor, and the application for registration prepared in the form prescribed by the Supreme Court Rules. Submit the application physically or through the electronic registration portal. The registration judge will review the legality of the incorporation. Once approved, the registration office issues the certificate of incorporation registration, and the Company acquires separate legal personality from the effective date of registration.
required_dossiers: Application for corporation incorporation registration
Notarized Articles of Incorporation
Capital deposit receipt from the bank
Minutes of the founding meeting
Personal seal certificates of all directors and the auditor
Proof of payment of the court registration fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registration court issues a supplemental order requesting additional documents or correction of minor discrepancies, the applicant must cure the identified defects and resubmit within the statutory response period, typically fourteen days, after which the court will complete the registration without restarting the entire review process.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Business Registration with the District Tax Office and Local Government for VAT and Corporate Income Tax
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: District Tax Office having jurisdiction over the Company's registered office and the local Gu office for municipal business licensing
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After incorporation registration is completed, apply for a business registration certificate from the competent District Tax Office, under the Resident Registration Number or corporate registration number, and also complete the necessary municipal business registration at the relevant local Gu office. Present the certificate of incorporation registration, corporate seal, lease contract for the registered office, and the first board resolution designating the statutory officers. The tax office will issue a business registration number reflecting a corporate taxable business. As the Company is engaged in pure digital services under ISIC 6311, no separate industrial or manufacturing operating license is required; however, the Company must maintain proper books and records for VAT, corporate income tax, and local tax withholdings.
required_dossiers: Certificate of corporation incorporation registration
Corporate seal certificate and specimen seal
Copy of the lease agreement for the registered office
First Board of Directors resolution appointing statutory officers
Application form for business registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the tax office or local Gu office requests supplemental documentation, such as a lease confirmation or registered address proof, the Company must file the supplementary materials within twenty days; after submission the tax office will issue the business registration certificate no later than five business days from the date of the supplemental filing.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not Applicable - Pure Digital Service under ISIC 6311

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) of the Republic of Korea - HomeTax electronic portal (www.hometax.go.kr); customs compliance through Korea Customs Service (unipass.customs.go.kr)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a foreign non-resident entity establishing a Korean place of business, the tax representative or branch manager must: 1) prepare a Business Registration Application (business registration number application form) and a Tax Representative Appointment Power of Attorney, 2) submit the foreign incorporation certificate, articles of incorporation, certificate of good standing from the foreign tax authority, and documentary proof of a domestic place of business or permanent establishment, 3) file the application with the competent district tax office of the NTS having jurisdiction over the domestic fixed place of business, 4) undergo NTS identity verification of the foreign representative, and 5) upon approval, receive the Business Registration Number certificate, which simultaneously serves as the VAT registration certificate; thereafter the entity must register for HomeTax e-tax invoice issuance and obtain a digital tax seal from an approved public certificate vendor.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None (no check-the-box election exists under Korean tax law; a Chusik Hoesa is always taxed as a separate corporate entity; hybrid mismatch adjustments under the International Tax Adjustment Act follow statutory classification without elective regimes)

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Zero - mandatory VAT registration for all corporations without a minimum economic turnover; simplified taxpayer regime available only to individual sole proprietors with annual taxable turnover below KRW 80,000,000
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory real-time electronic tax invoice issuance under Article 32 of the Korean VAT Act: billers must issue e-tax invoices through HomeTax or an NTS-approved ERP service provider, transmit them to the NTS no later than the next business day after the tax supply date, include the NTS-issued digital signature and verification code, and cooperate with NTS automated risk assessment; there is no fiscal stamping, but the transmission itself constitutes fiscal clearance for VAT deduction claims.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating applies to exported goods actually delivered out of Korea, overseas services (including digital content where the place of supply is outside Korea), international transport services, and other supplies expressly enumerated under Article 21 of the Korean VAT Act; the supplier must substantiate the export with Customs Service declaration, shipping documentation, and proof that consideration was received from an offshore customer in foreign currency through Korean foreign exchange banks; offshore B2B digital content and video match services qualify when the destination and actual consumption occur outside Korea, evidenced by customer IP/geo-location logs, subscriber country of residence, and payment origin.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Korea Customs Service Export Declaration (Export Declaration Confirmation/Bill of Entry equivalent)
Bill of Lading (B/L) or Airway Bill (AWB) evidencing physical or deemed cross-border shipment
Inward Remittance Certificate (Foreign Exchange Receipt Certificate) issued by the Korean designated foreign exchange bank evidencing foreign currency repatriation
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Fraudulent or unverified zero-rating claims are disallowed and recaptured along with interest, and additional penalties under Articles 25-2 and 29-3 of the VAT Act impose 40% of the evaded VAT for false returns; reckless or negligent misdeclaration triggers 20% penalties; criminal prosecution may follow under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act for willful tax fraud, and retrospective NTS reassessment can extend to 10 years for tax evasion cases.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Korea (BOK), with the Ministry of Economy and Finance as the foreign exchange policy authority under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: South Korea maintains a largely liberalised current-account convertibility regime under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act. KRW is freely convertible for legitimate trade, service, remittance and dividend payment once a foreign exchange declaration and standard purpose code are captured by a licensed foreign exchange bank. Capital-account transactions, however, are not fully deregulated: foreign direct investment into a Korean stock corporation requires a foreign investment report and bank-issued certificate of registration; intra-group loans, cross-border bond issuance and overseas securities transactions must be reported to the Ministry of Economy and Finance and the Bank of Korea with a demonstrable underlying economic purpose. Profit remittance is generally permitted after the company completes corporate tax filing and presents audited or internally reviewed financial statements, but the settlement bank will independently check outstanding local taxes, transfer-pricing substance and the existence of the operating revenue streams. For a digital social-app entity dependent on Apple IAP and Paymentwall, cross-border inflows must be classified as service export receipts, not capital remittances, to prevent the erroneous application of capital-market restrictions. The foreign exchange bank statement should match the corporate revenue ledger, and each payout should be traceable to a signed merchant settlement report.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: South Korea does not impose a mandatory percentage conversion of export proceeds into KRW. However, exporters must repatriate export foreign currency receipts to a foreign exchange account held with a licensed Korean foreign exchange bank within six months of the shipment date for goods or the service completion date for services, unless an extension has been granted by the Bank of Korea for documented business reasons. Once repatriated, the company may retain, convert or sell those funds freely through the licensed bank. For the video-matching service, the executed Apple Developer Agreement and Paymentwall Merchant Agreement, together with monthly payout statements and settlement reconciliations, must be retained as export evidence. Each USD credit to the corporate foreign currency account must be matched against the corresponding payout report and booked under the applicable service-receivables purpose code for foreign exchange reporting.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Corporate USD and KRW operating accounts, plus a dedicated capital escrow account for foreign investment verification
Basic operational currency account in KRW/USD with trade settlement and foreign exchange hedging capability, plus capital escrow sub-account
Basic operational KRW account with linked foreign currency demand deposit account and export proceeds collection module
Capital escrow account and multicurrency operational account for USD, EUR and KRW clearing, with documentary trade services

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Offshore digital EMI or neobank platforms such as Wise, Airwallex, Revolut Business or similar are not viable as the primary settlement banking layer for a Korean-resident Chusik Hoesa. Operating electronic money services, KRW IBAN-equivalent accounts and foreign exchange mediation within South Korea requires licensing under the Electronic Financial Transactions Act and registration under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act. None of the prominent foreign fintech EMIs possess such a licence to service domestic entities as a full-KRW current account provider. They may only be used as an auxiliary disbursement gateway if the licensed Korean Tier-1 bank enables the onward payment through its own approved international payment network. Unlicensed collection of KRW cross-border payments for a Korean video-based social app could be characterised as illegal foreign exchange brokerage and expose the treasury workflow to regulatory reversal and criminal prosecution.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: For a non-resident-owned Chusik Hoesa, the statutory director or an authorised Korean control person is normally required to appear physically at the chosen Korean bank branch for the initial corporate account opening. Remote consular proxy opening is not a routine service and is only tolerated in limited hardship cases where the bank can complete an in-branch identity verification of the proxy holder together with a recorded video interview of the foreign director. KEB Hana and Shinhan Bank are the most tolerant of an apostilled power-of-attorney structure, but they will still require the appointed representative to present original passports, corporate seal certificate and proof of authority at the branch. The enhanced onboarding procedure will include a live video KYC interview with the ultimate beneficial owner, review of the Korean lease or registered business address, and confirmation that the board resolution explicitly authorises the account signatories and the FX risk management mandate.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Ultimate beneficial ownership opacity in a foreign-owned Korean corporation with multiple offshore shareholders and no Korean tax resident shareholder
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarised and apostilled certificates of incorporation of every shareholder, a certified copy of the Chusik Hoesa share register, a UBO declaration chart illustrating each natural person, control percentage and source of wealth, passport copies of all beneficial owners, board resolutions approving equity ownership, and current proof of address for each shareholder.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-frequency low-value revenue streams from Apple IAP and Paymentwall producing a split-billing money trail that resembles smurfing, layering or unlicensed money transmission
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed Apple Developer Program Agreement and Paymentwall Merchant Agreement, monthly payout reconciliation reports, Apple and Paymentwall settlement currency breakdowns, chargeback history, an internal transaction monitoring and suspicious activity policy, a formal revenue recognition note explaining gross versus net settlement, and archived merchant invoices demonstrating the commercial relationship.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: The random-video-chat and cross-border social telephony model exposes the bank to adult-content risk, potential human trafficking proceeds, and sanctions evasion through overseas creators or end-users
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A detailed platform content compliance policy, AI moderation and screening logs, geo-blocking and sanctions-country restriction rules, identity verification records and KYB checks for overseas content creators, terms of service prohibiting illegal video content, a board-approved AML/CFT risk assessment for the video chat vertical, and any applicable data protection and online business registrations showing legal operation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident directors and remote signatories create a classic nominee-director red flag, particularly when the economic controller resides in a high-risk tax jurisdiction
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Apostilled board resolutions appointing the Korean resident controller and all bank signatories, a complete power-of-attorney chain ending at an identifiable natural person, original passports with entry stamps or visa documents, a Korean employment or resident registration arrangement for the local representativative, a physical Korean office lease or service office agreement, and a recorded video KYC interview transcript in which the foreign director confirms the purpose of the business and the identity of the ultimate beneficiary.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Foreign shareholders will inject equity through a registered foreign investment declaration filed with the Ministry of Economy and Finance and a licensed Korean foreign exchange bank. The SWIFT MT103 or MT202 instruction must carry the prescribed purpose code for foreign direct investment capital acquisition and identify the Korean entity as beneficiary. Funds are initially credited to a dedicated capital escrow account and cannot be commingled with operating revenue. After the bank verifies the foreign investment report, the certificate of foreign investment registration is issued and the funds may be converted into KRW at the current market rate without any mandatory surrender. The company must then complete capital verification through the bank and register the paid-in capital with the Korean corporate registry. Any subsequent increase must follow a new foreign investment report, and the original escrow records must be retained for at least five years for bank examination and regulatory audit.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For outbound trade and service disbursements, the primary rail is SWIFT MT103 for fees to overseas content creators, cloud infrastructure, advertising, Apple and Paymentwall related service providers, and other intangible service payments. Commercial letters of credit and standby letters of credit via SWIFT MT700/MT760 should be reserved for hardware procurement, platform device purchases or contractual merchandise trades where trade documents are required. Documentary collections may be used for non-recource trade transactions but are not suitable for pure digital service settlements. Each outbound KRW or USD transfer must be supported by an underlying contract, commercial invoice, settlement statement and a valid foreign exchange purpose code. The Korean bank will also perform a real-time check on overseas payee screening and will expect the treasury team to file a monthly statement of foreign exchange receipts and disbursements under the entity registration.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Short-term KRW/USD FX forward contracts for committed service receivables or payables with real underlying exposure and maximum tenor not exceeding twelve months

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) permitted only where the bank confirms a valid onshore/offshore position and where the transaction is not speculative, with full compliance with Bank of Korea position limits

Cross-currency swaps limited to hedging an outstanding foreign currency borrowing or long-term offshore financing liability, requiring prior bank approval and regulatory reporting through the Foreign Exchange Information System

Currency option or option-collared structures are excluded for this entity class unless a positive credit approval is obtained from the Tier-1 bank compliance committee after demonstrating a genuine hedge against FX volatility on the Apple and Paymentwall settlement flows

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax return (corporate tax base and tax amount report)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) of South Korea, filed through the HomeTax electronic filing system
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within the last day of the third month following the end of the fiscal year; for a calendar-year company, no later than March 31 of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing attracts 20% additional tax on the unreported or under-reported corporate income tax amount (40% if fraudulent); unpaid tax bears statutory overdue interest of 0.022% per day (approximately 8.03% per annum); continued non-payment allows NTS to attach bank accounts, receivables and assets, issue a public summons, close the business registration, and thereafter seek court dissolution or strike-off of a dormant company under Article 176 of the Korean Commercial Act.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Local corporate income tax surtax return and payment (10% local surtax on national corporate income tax)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Competent provincial/city local government, filed through the Local Tax System (WeTax) using the same national corporate tax return data
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Same deadline as the national corporate income tax return; March 31 for a December 31 fiscal year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to pay the local surtax by the deadline incurs a 20% negligent additional tax on the unpaid local tax plus daily overdue interest at the statutory local-tax rate (0.022% per day); continued delinquency triggers seizure and sale of corporate assets, public summons, and eventual administrative closure or deregistration of the business license.

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Free Economic Zone and Foreign Investment Zone tax holidays (100% CIT exemption for 5 years and 50% reduction for 2 years for qualifying foreign-invested corporations); R&D tax credits up to 30% for new growth source technologies; reduced progressive rates for taxable income below KRW 200 million; limited IP income exclusion under the Technology Fee Exclusion regime.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Korean Corporate Tax Return (CIT Act Article 60), Form 'Lawin Tax Base and Tax Computation Statement' (법인세 과세표준 및 세액계산서), filed electronically via the National Tax Service HomeTax portal.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within three months after the fiscal year-end (March 31 for calendar-year corporations); one-month extension available for corporations with independent audits or overseas subsidiaries.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 1 - Corporate Profile and Fiscal Year
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal form (Chusik Hoesa), tax ID, fiscal year-end, place of effective management, and shareholder directorship details.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Disclose all non-resident shareholders owning 5% or more and any foreign directors. A Korea-registered Chusik Hoesa is treated as a corporate tax resident of Korea; do not claim a foreign tax-home without a treaty tie-breaker analysis.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Aggregate Korean-source and global taxable income, carrying forward qualifying losses and applying permitted deductions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a foreign-owned Korean video chat app subsidiary, include Korean-source business income attributable to its domestic activities. Allocate profits under arm's-length standards and include any controlled foreign corporation (CFC) income imputed from untaxed offshore passive income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Detailed schedule of royalties, interest, management fees, and service fees paid or received with foreign related parties.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report every cross-border related-party transaction above KRW 100 million. Attach transfer pricing documentation evidencing comparable selection and arm's-length pricing. Absence of this schedule may trigger a 20% or 40% penalty and criminal referral.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Credit allowed for foreign taxes paid on income that is also subject to Korean corporate income tax.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only the Korean tax resident corporation may claim this credit for foreign taxes paid by a branch or PE. Do not include withholding taxes collected on dividends paid to non-resident shareholders; the shareholder must claim treaty relief separately.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 34 - Non-Resident Shareholder Distribution and Withholding Schedule
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Declaration of gross dividends and deemed distributions to non-resident shareholders, including calculated withholding tax and local surtax.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Withhold 20% national plus 2% local surtax on actual distributions. Treaty reductions require the beneficial owner's Tax Residency Certificate and a non-conduit declaration to be attached. The Korean paying company is liable for any short-withholding.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Self-assessed late filing, underreporting, negligent, or fraudulent penalties plus overdue interest.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If non-resident cross-border arrangements are hidden or the transfer pricing documentation is deficient, NTS will impose the maximum statutory penalty and list the responsible director as a restricted traveler. Disclose voluntary adjustments to mitigate civil penalties.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing triggers a 20% penalty on unpaid tax plus overdue interest of 0.022% per day; negligent underreporting triggers a 10% penalty; fraudulent underreporting triggers a 40% penalty under the Framework Act on National Taxes. Criminal tax evasion is punished under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act with imprisonment of up to 2 years (up to 7 years for aggravated cross-border evasion) and a fine of up to three times the evaded tax.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 22% (20% national corporate income tax withholding plus 2% local income surtax) on gross dividends paid to non-resident shareholders.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: The beneficial owner must submit a current-year Tax Residency Certificate (TRC), a signed beneficial ownership declaration, and evidence of no conduit or back-to-back arrangement to the Korean payor before payment. The payor files the Application for Exemption or Reduction of Non-Resident Tax under a Tax Treaty with the National Tax Service; NTS performs a substantive economic-substance review. If relief is not applied at source, the non-resident may file a reclaim with NTS within five years.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory WHT on non-resident royalties and interest is 22% (20% national plus 2% local). Under OECD-compliant DTAs, rates are commonly reduced to 0-15% for interest and 0-15% for royalties; dividends are often reduced to 5% or 10% for substantial shareholdings, and 15% for portfolio dividends, subject to TRC, beneficial ownership, and principal purpose test conditions.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: KRW 10 billion aggregate international related-party transactions for Local File documentation; KRW 100 billion consolidated group revenue for Master File and CbC Report threshold.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Korea applies substance-over-form under Article 4 of the International Tax Adjustment Act, permitting recharacterization or disregard of transactions lacking commercial rationale and economic substance. For treaty benefits, Korea applies a principal purpose test and requires core income-generating activities to be performed in Korea, including employees, premises, and decision-making functions. Although Korea does not have the Gulf ESR regime, a paper Chusik Hoesa with no domestic CIGA will be denied DTA relief and treated as a transparent or sham conduit.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion and Fraudulent Transfer Pricing
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Understating Korean-source income from the random video match app by routing subscriber payments through Paymentwall to an offshore zero-tax shell and filing the Korean CIT return without arm's-length consideration for intra-group technology licensing, data access royalties, or user acquisition services.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Punishment of Tax Evaders Act Article 3 and Corporate Income Tax Act Article 76-4: imprisonment up to 2 years (up to 7 years for aggravated evasion with cross-border concealment) and fines up to three times the evaded tax; administrative 40% fraudulent underreporting penalty under Framework Act on National Taxes Article 47-3; overdue interest of 0.022% per day.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: If corporate assets are insufficient, NTS pierces the veil under National Tax Collection Act Article 72 and holds directors jointly and severally liable for unpaid corporate tax and penalties. Directors may be issued no-departure orders, blacklisted as responsible officers, have personal bank accounts seized, and be imprisoned for willful participation in the evasion scheme.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating the Korean Chusik Hoesa as a paper corporation with no Korean employees, no board meetings, and no real substance, while claiming DTA-reduced withholding on outgoing royalties and dividends to an offshore beneficial owner that merely back-to-back licenses the app's intellectual property without local operational control.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: International Tax Adjustment Act Article 4 permits NTS to disregard the shell, attribute income to the actual non-resident enterprise, and deny treaty benefits; the company is reassessed at full statutory 22% WHT plus 20% underreporting penalty, and the foreign shareholder is treated as maintaining a Korean PE without appropriate registration.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are jointly and severally liable for the reassessed corporate taxes and unwithheld amounts. They may be additionally charged under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act for false declarations, subjected to travel bans, and face civil restitution of all distributed profits and compensation received from the shell.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML Non-Compliance and Money Laundering Through Video Chat App
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The directors knowingly permit the random video matching app to process proceeds of illegal adult content, fraud, or illicit matchmaking through Apple IAP and Paymentwall, and fail to perform customer due diligence, transaction monitoring, or suspicious transaction reporting to the Korean Financial Intelligence Unit (KoFIU) when individual remittances exceed KRW 10 million or exhibit a red-flag profile.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Act on Reporting and Using Specified Financial Transaction Information (FTRA) Article 50-5: fine up to KRW 50 million per violation and imprisonment up to 5 years for willful AML evasion; criminal proceeds are subject to asset forfeiture and confiscation under Criminal Act Article 48.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors with actual knowledge or willful blindness are personally arrested, criminally indicted, and may face asset seizure and confiscation. The corporate veil is pierced for restitution obligations, including disgorgement of dividends, salary, and profits obtained through the tainted payment flows; directors are also subject to international travel bans and extradition cooperation restrictions.
